articles.headline: Counsell says Cubs at disadvantage after schedule change
articles.description: Cubs manager Craig Counsell was quick to point out the disadvantages his team faces this weekend after the league moved Sunday's contest against the Boston Red Sox to Friday due to a poor weather forecast.
articles.body:
CHICAGO -- Cubs manager Craig Counsell was quick to point out the disadvantages his team faces this weekend after the league moved Sunday's contest against the Boston Red Sox to Friday due to a poor weather forecast. It means the two teams will play a doubleheader that night then conclude their regular seasons Saturday.

"They never move games up and especially within a five-day window of a starting rotation," Counsell said Wednesday. "So we can't have somebody ready to pitch on Saturday. They just moved games up on us. I understand there's extenuating circumstances, but you just don't see that happening."

Under normal circumstances, a rainout would force a doubleheader the next day, actually giving teams an extra day of rest for the starter of the postponed game. In this case, the Cubs will have to move Saturday's starter to Friday, leaving Game 162 in flux for them on the mound -- assuming weather doesn't cause havoc to Friday or Saturday's game in the first place.

It's likely lefty starter Shota Imanaga will pitch on short rest if Saturday's game is played as scheduled.

"What I know is happening is we're going to play three games," Counsell said. "So if weather is an issue, then yeah, we're going to have to figure out a place to play a third game."

The league discussed all options for the series as neither team wants to play Monday while moving it altogether to another city is a last resort. Both teams are likely to be in the postseason which starts Tuesday. Boston has already clinched a spot while the Cubs' magic number is one entering their contest against the Miami Marlins on Wednesday evening.

But seeding -- and home field advantage -- is still to be determined thus making the weekend series an important one. Adding some annoyance for Chicago is the fact that their season could be done while their closest competitors would have two more games to play, and league rules don't allow for an extra rostered player for September doubleheaders, further putting a burden on their pitching staff.

"The decision is made always on a balance of everybody's interest," Counsell stated. "And you get shortchanged in some ... or not have the optimal solution."

Meanwhile, Counsell is hopeful to have third baseman Alex Bregman in a game against his former team this weekend. Bregman spoke publicly for the first time on Wednesday since getting hit in the left cheek by a foul ball while on-deck on Sunday.

"It felt like I got hit by a baseball bat to the face," Bregman said. "The left side of my face has been numb. As soon as the swelling goes down, I'm sure I'll feel the breaks a little bit more."

Bregman's left eye is blood red while his cheek is still swollen but getting better. He said he can see fine and will continue to work his way back one "step at a time."

"There's a lot of fluid in my face over there," he explained. "If I move, the fluid moves. So if I'm bouncing up and down, my face feels like it's bouncing up and down."

articles.headline: Broncos RB Coleman doesn't practice; Dobbins, Harvey limited
articles.description: Broncos running backs J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey were limited in practice Wednesday, and Jonah Coleman did not practice. Nevertheless, coach Sean Payton said he thinks "we're going to be all right" at the position Sunday against the Rams.
articles.body:
ENGLEWOOD, Colo. -- Ahead of a primetime matchup with the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday, the Denver Broncos practiced Wednesday with three of their four running backs either limited or out of practice, with coach Sean Payton saying he still hoped for the best.

J.K. Dobbins, who left Sunday's win over the Jacksonville Jaguars in the third quarter with a left hamstring injury, and RJ Harvey, who did not play Sunday because of a hamstring injury he suffered in the season opener, were both limited in practice.

And rookie Jonah Coleman did not practice. Coleman sprained an ankle during Sunday's game, but he stayed in the lineup and was the running back on the field to help the Broncos seal the win. He had 33 of his 39 rushing yards, including two 12-yard runs, on the Broncos' final possession, when the offense used up the final 4:41 on the clock.

Asked Wednesday if he had concerns about the position heading into Sunday's game, Payton didn't offer details about the injuries, but added, "I think we're good at that position ... I think we're going to be all right.''

Tyler Badie was the only running back on the active roster who was a full participant in Wednesday's practice. Fullback Adam Prentice and running back Cody Schrader, the team's leading rusher in the preseason, are on the Broncos' practice squad.

Coleman, a fourth-round pick in the 2026 draft, had his first career touchdown on a 3-yard run against the Jaguars. He has received treatment on the injured ankle over the past three days and that will continue through the week.

Dobbins, who leads the Broncos in carries (18) and yards rushing (72) through two games, missed seven games in 2025 after he suffered a season-ending foot injury in Week 10. He had issued a "pinky swear'' promise in training camp that he would play every game this season.

The Broncos did work out three running backs Tuesday -- Jaden Nixon, Sam Scott and Marcus Yarns -- but as of Wednesday had not signed any of the three.

Prentice has already been elevated from the practice squad twice this season for games, so he has one more elevation remaining before the Broncos would have to sign him to the roster to have him available for games.

articles.headline: UK PM Burnham wants 'outdated' football drinking ban scrapped
articles.description: A ban on football fans drinking in the stands during matches is outdated, discriminatory and should be scrapped, Andy Burnham said.
articles.body:
A ban on football fans drinking in the stands during matches is outdated, discriminatory and should be scrapped, Andy Burnham said.

The Prime Minister said it was unfair for football fans to be singled out when supporters of other sports were able to drink while watching their teams.

The ban was put in place during the 1980s when concerns about hooliganism were at their height and covers the top-five tiers of English men's football.

But Everton fan Mr. Burnham said it was a measure from "an era when football was very different."

The Football Supporters' Association (FSA) welcomed the Prime Minister's words and said successful pilots of alcohol in the stands had been carried out in the women's game.

But police chiefs warned it would be "incredibly rash" to make changes without proper consultation with forces.

Mr. Burnham told reporters: "I don't think it's fair for football fans to be singled out in that way and I made that point.

"I think that legislation dates to an era where football was very different.

"And I do believe there is a case to remove that discrimination. There are different ways it could be done, perhaps on a trial basis.

"But I'm not going to back away from what's been a long-held view of mine. I don't see how it can be fair that some supporters of one sport can be treated differently from others."

The Sporting Events (Control of Alcohol) Act 1985 prohibits drinking in sight of the pitch in England and Wales in the top-five men's leagues.

FSA chairman Tom Greatrex said: "The FSA has always argued that it's unfair to criminalise football fans for having a pint while watching the match -- especially since you can sit in the same seat drinking alcohol whilst watching an Oasis gig or rugby league.

"Many clubs are in favour as well. WSL and WSL2 ran a successful pilot, meaning fans can now drink in the stands at many grounds, while the EFL has long supported a trial.

"We welcome the Prime Minister's comments and totally agree that the legislation is outdated and deserves to be reviewed. We look forward to being part of that consultation."

A UK Football Policing Unit spokesman said police chiefs would welcome a meeting with Mr. Burnham to "explain the challenges these proposed changes would bring to policing and the safety of staff and fans."

The spokesman said: "Other sports simply don't see the violence and criminal behaviour from their supporters that football does, albeit a minority, with alcohol often playing a significant part in violent and disorderly behaviour.

"It would be irresponsible to fuel this by allowing greater alcohol consumption during games.

"Following a number of football-related tragedies, changes in legislation were implemented after the Taylor Report for good reason and we are currently in the longest ever period without a significant football-related disaster.

articles.headline: Eric Cantona 'wouldn't have joined' Man United if Jim Ratcliffe had been in charge in the 1990s
articles.description: Manchester United great Eric Cantona has said he would never have joined the club had current co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe been in charge.
articles.body:
Manchester United great Eric Cantona has said he would never have joined the club had current co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe been in charge.

Ratcliffe has courted more controversy this week, saying in a BBC interview that the United Kingdom is in decline because "nobody's tough enough to deal with the immigration problem."

France forward Cantona has previously been named by Ratcliffe as his favourite United player.

But when United fan Pete Boyle, on his TikTok channel, asked Cantona if he would have signed for the club under Ratcliffe, he replied: "No, Of course not.

"You know what I think about all of this, with this kind of politics and I cannot understand that someone like this can say something like this when he's one of the owners of the club.

"Football is a very popular sport. Football is made -- all the greatest players come from different waves of immigration. Everywhere, in France, in England, everywhere.

- Benjamin Šeško vows to 'fully dedicate' himself to recovery after Man United injury setback

"In France for instance, the greatest players in France, they all come from different waves of immigration."

Cantona moved to Old Trafford in 1992 from rivals Leeds and helped the club win four Premier League titles in five seasons.

articles.headline: 49ers place starting DT C.J. West on IR due to knee injury
articles.description: 49ers defensive tackle C.J. West, who is going to miss at least a chunk of the season with a bone chip in his knee that will require surgery, was placed on injured reserve Wednesday.
articles.body:
SANTA CLARA, Calif. -- Add defensive tackle to the list of positions where the San Francisco 49ers are growing thin after the team placed starting nose tackle C.J. West on injured reserve Wednesday.

On the heels of a season-ending patellar injury to Alfred Collins and a high ankle sprain for rookie James Thompson Jr., West is going to miss at least a chunk of the season with a bone chip in his knee that will require surgery.

Coach Kyle Shanahan said West's injury is not season-ending, but it is another blow to a position that has just two healthy players remaining from the five that originally made the 53-man roster.

The Niners didn't initially list West among their injuries coming out of their Week 2 win against the Miami Dolphins, but Shanahan said West's knee has been battling "something" since training camp.

"I don't know if this is the same or if it was something new," Shanahan said. "But it was bothering him a lot after the game."

There's no timeline for West's return, but the 49ers added more depth at defensive tackle Wednesday. San Francisco signed veteran Naquan Jones, who has played in 60 games with eight starts for the Tennessee Titans, Arizona Cardinals and Houston Texans, off the Minnesota Vikings' practice squad.

Jones, who projects as more of a nose tackle and a direct replacement for West, took part in his first practice with the Niners on Wednesday afternoon. As it stands, the Niners have just three healthy defensive tackles -- Osa Odighizuwa, Gracen Halton and Jones -- on the roster.

San Francisco also has three more defensive tackles on the practice squad in Kevin Givens, Sebastian Valdez and McKinnley Jackson. Defensive end Keion White also can move inside to tackle in obvious passing situations.

For now, Shanahan said the Niners will evaluate those practice squad options to see who else can help fill in for West.

"Anytime you have five D tackles make a team and you're down to two of them after two games, that's always a concern for anybody," Shanahan said. "We were able to sign one new guy and then we got three guys on practice squad that will be competing to see who's up. We got guys there in this building, so we got to see how those guys step it up."

As for another injury-ravaged position, the Niners signed veteran receiver Brandin Cooks to the practice squad Wednesday. Cooks' arrival coincides with a high ankle sprain for Demarcus Robinson as well as a sore hip for Mike Evans that left the Niners without either participating in Wednesday's practice.

Robinson will miss three to six weeks and could land on injured reserve, while the Niners plan to manage Evans this week with hopes he will play Sunday against the Arizona Cardinals. San Francisco is also without Ricky Pearsall (knee, out for the season) and De'Zhaun Stribling (ankle, currently on IR).

articles.headline: Dodgers' Shohei Ohtani returns from IL stint, starts vs. Padres
articles.description: Dodgers star Shohei Ohtani, who was on the injured list since Sept. 8, was activated and in the starting lineup for Wednesday's game against the Padres.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Dodgers star Shohei Ohtani, who was on the injured list since Sept. 8, was activated and in the starting lineup for Wednesday's game against the San Diego Padres.

The designated hitter will bat second, with Mookie Betts, who is hitting.373/.468/.746 in September, leading off against Padres left-hander Robbie Ray.

Ohtani was put on the IL because of lingering pain in his right biceps and left knee. He will only hit the rest of this season.

The Dodgers also optioned outfielder Josue De Paula to Triple-A Oklahoma City. He had 10 hits and 11 walks in 42 plate appearances since temporarily replacing Ohtani at designated hitter.

De Paula is strongly being considered as an option to be a left-handed bat off the bench during the postseason.

The Dodgers on Tuesday had activated right-hander Roki Sasaki and center fielder Andy Pages off the IL.

ESPN's Alden Gonzalez contributed to this report.

articles.headline: McVay says Nacua's injury not 'long-term' concern, but Rams being cautious
articles.description: Rams coach Sean McVay said receiver Puka Nacua does not have a hernia, but the team will "err on the side of caution" with the injury.
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES -- Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay said he's not sure whether Puka Nacua will play in Week 3, but the team is not worried that the wide receiver's injury will be "any sort of long-term threat."

Nacua did not play Monday night with what was listed as a hip injury on the injury report, but McVay later clarified that Nacua was dealing with "a little bit of soreness" in his groin.

McVay said Nacua does not have a hernia, but the team is being cautious with the injury.

"When you're a skill player and you're really trying to hit high-speed yards and really open up and you feel just ... it's like some of the things that can almost be like pre-hernia is kind of what he's feeling," McVay said. "And so you err on the side of caution. Usually time is the best thing that allows that thing to heal. And then once you get to a certain point, then I think you feel pretty good moving forward."

The Rams did not practice Wednesday, instead holding a walk-through on the short week, but the team estimated that Nacua would not have taken part if it had. McVay said the team will see whether Nacua will practice Thursday, adding that he knows Nacua is "frustrated" with the situation.

"We all want him to be able to be out there, but we want him to be able to return to performance, not just be able to just kind of gut through it," McVay said.

Last week, McVay said Nacua's injury wasn't related to the psoas injury that caused him to miss time in August. In the Rams' season opener, Nacua led Los Angeles with five catches for 74 yards on nine targets.

The Rams play the Denver Broncos in Week 3 on "Sunday Night Football."

articles.headline: Walker Jenkins' pinch-hit RBI single in the 7th keys Twins' 4-2 victory over Giants
articles.description: — Pinch-hitter Walker Jenkins hit an RBI single in the seventh inning that put Minnesota ahead and the Twins won their second straight over the San Francisco Giants with a 4-2 victory on Wednesday.
articles.body:
SAN FRANCISCO -- — Pinch-hitter Walker Jenkins hit an RBI single in the seventh inning that put Minnesota ahead and the Twins won their second straight over the San Francisco Giants with a 4-2 victory on Wednesday.


              The score was 2-all with Kody Clemens at second and one out in the seventh. Jenkins delivered a base hit to right off Dylan Smith (0-6) that scored Clemens for a 3-2 Minnesota lead. With two outs, Josh Bell added an RBI single off Sam Hentges to increase the Twins’ edge to 4-2.


              Yoendrys Gomez (3-4) retired all five hitters he faced to earn the win. Andrew Morris worked a scoreless ninth for his fifth save. He struck out Shay Whitcomb with runners at first and second to end the game. 


              Minnesota got on the board first when Luke Keaschall took Cesar Perdomo deep to left for a solo homer in the third inning. It was Keaschall’s 10th homer of the season.


              The Giants scored both of their runs with two outs in the fourth on Whitcomb’s pop-fly single that fell just fair near the right-field line. It gave San Francisco a 2-1 advantage.


              The Twins tied it in the fifth on Keaschall’s sacrifice fly that scored Ben Ross, who had tripled.


              Perdomo, a rookie left-hander, gave up two runs on five hits in 5 1/3 innings. He struck out two and did not issue a walk.


              Minnesota starter Connor Prielipp, also a rookie left-hander, allowed two runs on four hits in 5 1/3 innings. He struck out three and walked two.


              With the loss, the Giants fell to 37-41 at home, meaning they will have a losing record for the season at Oracle Park. 


              Up next
              Twins RHP Joe Ryan (6-10, 3.83 ERA) faces the visiting Rangers on Friday night.


              Giants RHP Yunior Marte (0-1, 4.66) takes on the visiting Dodgers on Friday night.

articles.headline: Judge says he intends to be available for AL Wild Card Series
articles.description: Yankees' slugger Aaron Judge told ESPN on Wednesday that he intends to be ready for Game 1 of the AL Wild Card Series at Yankee Stadium next Tuesday.
articles.body:
NEW YORK -- New York Yankees star Aaron Judge is not giving up on being available for the start of the postseason.

The three-time MVP told ESPN on Wednesday that he intends to be ready for Game 1 of the AL Wild Card Series at Yankee Stadium next Tuesday.

"That's what the plan is," Judge said. "Try to get my body ready so I'm ready to go."

Judge was placed on the injured list Saturday with a right calf strain, ending his regular season. He later specified that the strain is in the soleus muscle, which he noted is essential for running and hitting. He confirmed that he received a PPP injection Monday and was waiting for clearance to resume activity that involved the leg.

On Tuesday, Yankees manager Aaron Boone said he does not expect to have Judge available for the wild-card series, though he did not rule out the possibility.

"We're planning on him not being a part of that," Boone said.

Judge, 34, said he has had discussions with decision-makers in the organization about his prognosis, which has not been made clear publicly.

"We've done a lot of talks, but I can't control what people say," Judge said. "So you'll have to talk to them about that."

Asked if he expects to be on the roster, Judge said he didn't know.

"I don't make the roster," Judge said. "I've got no idea."

Judge said he suffered the injury during the Yankees' 5-4 loss to the Minnesota Twins on Sept. 16, in his seventh game back after missing more than three months with a fractured rib. He and the club were initially hopeful that it was minor, but he underwent an MRI on Thursday that revealed the strain.

Judge went 4-for-23 with 13 strikeouts, one walk and one home run in 24 plate appearances after returning from his fractured rib without a rehab assignment. Overall, he batted .241 with 18 home runs and an .871 OPS in 66 games, which includes playing with the fractured rib for over a month until late May.

The Yankees went 41-25 and averaged 5.12 runs with Judge in the lineup this season. Entering Wednesday, they're 49-42 and averaging 4.15 runs without him. They will likely face the Boston Red Sox in the wild-card series for the second consecutive postseason after knocking out their rivals in three games with Judge in their lineup last October.

"We've got games to win," Judge said. "I'm getting paid to play games for the New York Yankees, so I'll get back as soon as I can."
